files.purpose: The XcodeGen-generated Xcode project file for the single macOS app target DroppyCode: it declares the app product, the SwiftTerm SPM dependency, the three resource files copied into the bundle, and the four XCBuildConfiguration blocks (project Debug/Release and target Debug/Release) that hold every literal build setting the shipped app is compiled with.
key_symbols: PBXFileSystemSynchronizedRootGroup D316607E993AEB4CB4FF2F06 /* DroppyCode */ (path DroppyCode, empty explicitFileTypes and explicitFolders)
PBXSourcesBuildPhase 6FB0B0F54C3B5B2B02EA0E7E (files list EMPTY; sources come from the synchronized folder)
calls_into: https://github.com/migueldeicaza/SwiftTerm at exactVersion 1.20.0; the SwiftTerm product is linked in PBXFrameworksBuildPhase
DroppyCode/App/Window/DroppyCode-Bridging-Header.h via SWIFT_OBJC_BRIDGING_HEADER on both target configs
AppIcon asset catalog entry via ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_APPICON_NAME on both target configs
LICENSE, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and TRADEMARK.md at the repo root, copied as bundle resources
project.yml, the XcodeGen spec this file is generated from
state_owned: objects dictionary keyed by 24-hex XcodeGen-deterministic object ids
Both build phases use buildActionMask = 2147483647 and runOnlyForDeploymentPostprocessing = 0
side_effects: Resources build phase copies LICENSE, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and TRADEMARK.md into the built DroppyCode.app bundle
Frameworks build phase links the SwiftTerm SPM product, which triggers a package fetch and resolve at build time
Release target config signs with CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY = "Developer ID Application" and CODE_SIGN_STYLE = Manual (Developer ID distribution, not the App Store)
ENABLE_HARDENED_RUNTIME = YES on both target configs, a notarization prerequisite
GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE = YES synthesizes Info.plist from the INFOPLIST_KEY_* settings at build time
Release project config emits a dSYM because DEBUG_INFORMATION_FORMAT = "dwarf-with-dsym"
platform_assumptions: SDKROOT = macosx on project and target configs; macOS only, no iOS or Catalyst slice
MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET = 26.0 in both project configs; requires macOS 26 APIs
ARCHS = arm64 with EXCLUDED_ARCHS = x86_64; Apple Silicon only, no Intel and no universal binary
SWIFT_VERSION = 6.0 with SWIFT_APPROACHABLE_CONCURRENCY = YES (Swift 6 strict concurrency in approachable mode)
SWIFT_OBJC_BRIDGING_HEADER implies AppKit/Objective-C interop in DroppyCode/App/Window
COMBINE_HIDPI_IMAGES = YES, a classic macOS-only TIFF HiDPI image combining setting
LD_RUNPATH_SEARCH_PATHS includes @executable_path/../Frameworks, the macOS .app bundle layout
objectVersion 77 and preferredProjectObjectVersion 77 require Xcode 16 or newer for file-system-synchronized groups
Metal toolchain assumed present (MTL_ENABLE_DEBUG_INFO, MTL_FAST_MATH = YES)
DEVELOPMENT_TEAM = NARHG44L48 is an Apple Developer team identifier
persisted_fields: PRODUCT_NAME = "Droppy Code" (Release target), "Droppy Code Dev" (Debug target), "$(TARGET_NAME)" (both project configs)
ui_elements: INFOPLIST_KEY_CFBundleDisplayName = "Droppy Code" (Release target config), the name shown in Finder, the Dock and the menu bar
INFOPLIST_KEY_CFBundleDisplayName = "Droppy Code Dev" (Debug target config), so dev builds are visibly distinct
INFOPLIST_KEY_NSHumanReadableCopyright = "Droppy Code, the coding app by Droppy. MIT License.", the copyright line in the standard About panel
LICENSE, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and TRADEMARK.md shipped as resources so the app can display them in-app
feature_notes: Debug and Release differ by identity, not only optimization: Debug installs as iordv.droppycode.dev named "Droppy Code Dev" with CODE_SIGN_STYLE = Automatic; Release installs as iordv.droppycode named "Droppy Code" with CODE_SIGN_STYLE = Manual and CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY = "Developer ID Application"

Project Debug config literals: GCC_OPTIMIZATION_LEVEL = 0, SWIFT_OPTIMIZATION_LEVEL = "-Onone", SWIFT_ACTIVE_COMPILATION_CONDITIONS = DEBUG, GCC_PREPROCESSOR_DEFINITIONS = ("$(inherited)", "DEBUG=1"), ENABLE_TESTABILITY = YES, ONLY_ACTIVE_ARCH = YES, DEBUG_INFORMATION_FORMAT = dwarf, MTL_ENABLE_DEBUG_INFO = INCLUDE_SOURCE, GCC_DYNAMIC_NO_PIC = NO

Project Release config literals: SWIFT_OPTIMIZATION_LEVEL = "-O", SWIFT_COMPILATION_MODE = wholemodule, ENABLE_NS_ASSERTIONS = NO, DEBUG_INFORMATION_FORMAT = "dwarf-with-dsym", MTL_ENABLE_DEBUG_INFO = NO; Release carries no ENABLE_TESTABILITY and no ONLY_ACTIVE_ARCH key at all
DEAD_CODE_STRIPPING = YES on BOTH target configs including Debug, so debug builds do not keep unreferenced symbols
No test target, no test bundle and no PBXTargetDependency appears anywhere in the file; the project builds exactly one product
The Sources build phase files list is literally empty; all Swift sources arrive via fileSystemSynchronizedGroups pointing at the DroppyCode folder, so adding a .swift file needs no project edit

Warning posture is Apple template defaults with three escalated to errors: CLANG_WARN_DIRECT_OBJC_ISA_USAGE = YES_ERROR, CLANG_WARN_OBJC_ROOT_CLASS = YES_ERROR, GCC_WARN_ABOUT_RETURN_TYPE = YES_ERROR; plus CLANG_WARN_UNGUARDED_AVAILABILITY = YES_AGGRESSIVE, GCC_WARN_UNINITIALIZED_AUTOS = YES_AGGRESSIVE and CLANG_ANALYZER_NUMBER_OBJECT_CONVERSION = YES_AGGRESSIVE
CLANG_CXX_LANGUAGE_STANDARD = "gnu++14", CLANG_CXX_LIBRARY = "libc++", GCC_C_LANGUAGE_STANDARD = gnu11 are boilerplate; no C or C++ source belongs to the target
COPY_PHASE_STRIP = NO in BOTH project configs, so the Release binary is not stripped during the copy phase
SwiftTerm is pinned with requirement kind = exactVersion, version = 1.20.0, not a range, so the terminal emulator version is locked

CLANG_ENABLE_MODULES, CLANG_ENABLE_OBJC_ARC and CLANG_ENABLE_OBJC_WEAK are all YES in both project configs, and ENABLE_STRICT_OBJC_MSGSEND = YES, ALWAYS_SEARCH_USER_PATHS = NO, GCC_NO_COMMON_BLOCKS = YES
unresolved_questions: Whether DroppyCode.app is ever built as a universal binary for release: this pinned file hard-excludes x86_64, but a CI script outside this bundle could override ARCHS

LastUpgradeCheck = 1430 is stale relative to objectVersion 77 and a macOS 26 deployment target; it looks like XcodeGen boilerplate with no observable effect, but I cannot confirm that from this file alone

Where the shipped LICENSE, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and TRADEMARK.md resources are read and displayed; only the project.yml comment names an About Licenses screen and the reading code is not in this bundle

files.purpose: The implicit workspace embedded inside DroppyCode.xcodeproj, declaring exactly one FileRef pointing at the project itself (location = "self:"); it exists so Xcode has a workspace to hang the shared SwiftPM Package.resolved off.
calls_into: the sibling xcshareddata/swiftpm/Package.resolved that lives under this workspace
state_owned: a single FileRef entry whose only attribute is location = "self:"
side_effects: None; it is a declarative XML manifest Xcode reads when opening the project
platform_assumptions: Xcode-specific workspace format, meaningless outside Apple's toolchain and with no Windows equivalent
feature_notes: There is no separate .xcworkspace at the repo root; the only workspace is this auto-generated in-project one, so the app is opened via DroppyCode.xcodeproj directly
Because only self: is listed, no sibling projects and no local Swift packages participate in the build
Written in Xcode's own style: 3-space indentation and spaced attribute assignment (location = "self:"), and FileRef uses an explicit closing tag rather than self-closing
unresolved_questions: Whether this file is regenerated by XcodeGen or preserved verbatim from Xcode; project.yml does not mention it and nothing in this bundle lists it as an XcodeGen output

files.purpose: The checked-in SwiftPM resolution lockfile for the Xcode project: it pins the exact git revisions of the two packages in the dependency graph, SwiftTerm and its transitive swift-argument-parser, so every build of Droppy Code links identical terminal-emulator code.
calls_into: XCRemoteSwiftPackageReference "SwiftTerm" in project.pbxproj, whose exactVersion 1.20.0 requirement this resolution satisfies
state_owned: pins array with 2 entries, ordered by identity
a per-pin state object holding revision and version
side_effects: Drives git clones and checkouts of both GitHub repositories into DerivedData during resolution, so a build on a machine without them cached needs network access
platform_assumptions: Apple SwiftPM and Xcode resolution format; Windows has no equivalent, so the port must substitute a Windows terminal backend for SwiftTerm rather than translate this file
feature_notes: SwiftTerm 1.20.0 is the only direct third-party dependency of the app; everything else is Apple system frameworks
swift-argument-parser 1.8.2 is transitive, pulled in through SwiftTerm; project.pbxproj declares no XCSwiftPackageProductDependency on it
Both pins carry an explicit semver version string, so neither is a branch pin or a bare-revision pin
Formatting is Xcode's JSON writer style: 2-space indentation, a space before every colon, and keys in the order originHash, pins, version
unresolved_questions: Whether any swift-argument-parser code ends up inside the shipped .app: it is resolved and pinned, but only the SwiftTerm product is listed in PBXFrameworksBuildPhase, and SwiftTerm's own Package.swift target graph is not in this bundle

files.purpose: The XcodeGen specification that is the real source of truth for the Droppy Code build: it declares the single macOS application target, the synced-folder source layout, the SwiftTerm package, the shared base settings and the Debug/Release overrides from which DroppyCode.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj is generated.
key_symbols: targets.DroppyCode.sources (synced folder plus three resource paths)
calls_into: the DroppyCode/ source folder, declared with type: syncedFolder
LICENSE, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and TRADEMARK.md, each with buildPhase: resources
the AppIcon entry in the asset catalog

target settings.base: PRODUCT_NAME, PRODUCT_MODULE_NAME, PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER, GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE, three INFOPLIST_KEY_* values, ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_APPICON_NAME, ENABLE_HARDENED_RUNTIME, CODE_SIGN_STYLE, DEAD_CODE_STRIPPING, SWIFT_OBJC_BRIDGING_HEADER
side_effects: Running xcodegen rewrites DroppyCode.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj wholesale from this spec
buildPhase: resources entries cause LICENSE, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and TRADEMARK.md to be copied into the app bundle
Declaring the SwiftTerm package makes Xcode resolve and fetch it over the network
platform_assumptions: platform: macOS with options.deploymentTarget.macOS "26.0", so macOS 26 is the minimum
ARCHS: arm64 plus EXCLUDED_ARCHS: x86_64, Apple Silicon only
SWIFT_VERSION "6.0" with SWIFT_APPROACHABLE_CONCURRENCY, the Swift 6 concurrency model
CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY: Developer ID Application together with ENABLE_HARDENED_RUNTIME: YES means Apple notarized direct distribution outside the Mac App Store
XcodeGen's syncedFolder source type requires a recent XcodeGen and the Xcode 16+ project format
persisted_fields: PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER: iordv.droppycode (base), overridden to iordv.droppycode.dev in the Debug config
PRODUCT_MODULE_NAME: DroppyCode, constant across configs so the Swift module name never changes
ui_elements: INFOPLIST_KEY_CFBundleDisplayName: "Droppy Code" in base, overridden to "Droppy Code Dev" in Debug
PRODUCT_NAME: "Droppy Code" in base, overridden to "Droppy Code Dev" in Debug; note the space in the product name versus the spaceless DroppyCode module name
INFOPLIST_KEY_NSHumanReadableCopyright: "Droppy Code, the coding app by Droppy. MIT License."
INFOPLIST_KEY_LSApplicationCategoryType: public.app-category.developer-tools, written unquoted here and quoted in the generated pbxproj
feature_notes: The only prose in the file is the comment above the three resource entries: "The license, the third-party notices and the trademark policy travel with every copy of the app; About shows them under Licenses." It states an in-app About requirement the port must honor
The Debug config overrides exactly three keys (PRODUCT_NAME, PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER, INFOPLIST_KEY_CFBundleDisplayName) so a dev build coexists with the release build on one Mac
The Release config overrides exactly two keys (CODE_SIGN_STYLE: Manual, CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY: Developer ID Application); base CODE_SIGN_STYLE is Automatic, which therefore applies to Debug
DEAD_CODE_STRIPPING: YES sits in the target's settings.base, so it applies to Debug as well as Release; it is not a release-only optimization
The spec declares no test target, no app extension, no helper tool and no scheme customization; the entire product is one app
sources uses type: syncedFolder for DroppyCode, which is exactly why the generated Sources build phase has an empty files list
Only this file carries MARKETING_VERSION 1.6.0 and CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION 19 as authored values; the app version is bumped by editing project.yml, not the pbxproj

Settings present in the generated pbxproj but absent from this spec (COMBINE_HIDPI_IMAGES, LD_RUNPATH_SEARCH_PATHS, SDKROOT, the entire CLANG_/GCC_ warning block, MTL_*, SWIFT_COMPILATION_MODE, DEBUG_INFORMATION_FORMAT, COPY_PHASE_STRIP) are XcodeGen defaults rather than authored choices
unresolved_questions: Whether an XcodeGen version is pinned anywhere (Makefile, Brewfile, CI workflow); nothing in this bundle records which XcodeGen produced the committed pbxproj
Whether project.yml or the committed project.pbxproj is treated as canonical day to day, since both are checked in and can drift
The file has CRLF line endings in this checkout, which may be a Windows git autocrlf artifact rather than the upstream committed form; I cannot tell from the working tree alone
